author: Robert Carr
description: Chicken and hominy in a roasted tomatillo-poblano broth thickened with toasted pumpkin seeds. Cooking down the green puree gives the soup a deep savory base before cilantro and a restrained lime finish.
equipment: 8-quart Dutch oven or heavy soup pot
Broiler-safe rimmed sheet pan and foil
Blender approved for warm liquids with a vented lid

ingredients: 2 lb (907 g) unbrined boneless skinless chicken breast; halve thick breasts horizontally into cutlets no thicker than 3/4 inch
1 1/2 lb (680 g) tomatillos after husking, rinsed and halved
2 poblano peppers (about 300 g), halved, stems and seeds removed
1 jalapeno (about 15 g), halved, stem, seeds and pale ribs removed
1 large white onion (300 g peeled), cut into 1/2-inch wedges
6 garlic cloves, left in their skins for roasting; about 20 g peeled yield
1 cup (32 g) cilantro leaves and tender stems, divided into two 1/2-cup portions
6 cups (1.44 L) low-sodium chicken broth, with 70 mg sodium or less per cup, divided into 1 cup and 5 cups
2 cans (15.5 oz each) white hominy, drained and rinsed; about 500 g total
instructions: Set an oven rack about 6 inches below the broiler and heat the broiler to high. Line a broiler-safe sheet pan with foil, not parchment. Arrange 1 1/2 lb (680 g) halved tomatillos, 2 halved poblanos (300 g), 1 halved jalapeno (15 g), 1 white onion cut into wedges (300 g), and 6 skin-on garlic cloves (20 g peeled yield) in a single layer, with pepper skins upward. Broil for 10-15 minutes until softened and blistered in spots. Turn the onion once, and remove garlic cloves as soon as they soften, usually after 5-8 minutes; do not let the garlic burn.

While the vegetables broil, toast 1/2 cup (60 g) raw pepitas in the dry soup pot over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently, until fragrant and lightly golden. Transfer to a plate immediately so they do not scorch.

Let the roasted vegetables cool for 5 minutes. Peel the 6 roasted garlic cloves and remove any loose, blackened pepper skin. Transfer all roasted vegetables and their pan juices to a blender, together with the toasted 1/2 cup (60 g) pepitas, 1/2 cup (16 g) cilantro, and 1 cup (240 mL) chicken broth. Blend until mostly smooth. Use a blender rated for warm liquids, leave headroom and vent its lid according to its instructions; do not use a sealed personal-blender cup with hot ingredients.

Heat 1 tbsp (13.5 g) olive oil in the pot over medium heat. Add 1 tsp cumin and 2 tsp crumbled Mexican oregano; stir for 20 seconds. Carefully pour in the complete green puree from the previous step; it may splatter. Cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring frequently, until slightly thickened and the aroma is roasted and savory rather than raw and grassy.

Add 5 cups (1.2 L) chicken broth, about 500 g drained hominy from 2 cans, 1/4 tsp (1.5 g) fine sea salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper. Bring just to a simmer. Lower in 2 lb (907 g) chicken cutlets, submerge them and return to a gentle simmer. Cook for 12-18 minutes, turning once, until each cutlet reaches 165 F (74 C) in its thickest part. Remove individual pieces as they reach temperature rather than continuing to cook the thinner ones.

Transfer the cooked chicken from the 907 g raw batch to a clean board and shred into bite-size pieces. Turn off the heat, return all shredded chicken to the pot, and stir in 2 tbsp (30 mL) lime juice and 1/2 cup (16 g) cilantro. Rest for 5 minutes. Stir thoroughly and divide the complete batch evenly among 6 servings, distributing chicken and hominy evenly. Do not boil the shredded chicken for another 10 minutes; it has already reached its safe cooking temperature.
notes: Flavor: roast the green vegetables, toast the pepitas and cook down the blended puree before adding the bulk of the broth. These are separate flavor-building steps, not optional decoration. Lime is deliberately restrained because tomatillos already provide acidity. Poblanos and jalapenos vary in heat even after trimming.

Health-conscious design: lean unbrined chicken, vegetables, unsalted seeds, measured olive oil and modest added salt. Canned hominy can be quite salty; compare labels and drain and rinse it. Rinsing does not make hominy sodium-free, and no fixed sodium-reduction percentage is assumed. This soup is not certified low sodium.

Use fully cooked canned hominy, not dried hominy or ordinary sweetcorn; dried hominy needs a different preparation. Use the contents of both drained cans even if the actual drained yield differs slightly from 500 g. Optional shredded cabbage and radish can be served separately for crunch, but are not included in this base recipe or its grocery list.

Meal prep: divide into 6 shallow containers rather than cooling the full pot on the counter. Refrigerate at 40 F (4 C) or below within 2 hours, or within 1 hour above 90 F (32 C). Use refrigerated portions within 3-4 days. Freeze portions intended for later days on prep day, leaving headroom, and plan to use them within 3 months for quality. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

Reheat one portion with 2 tbsp (30 mL) water, stirring, until the soup briefly reaches a rolling boil and the chicken and center reach 165 F (74 C). Avoid prolonged boiling once hot. For microwave reheating, cover loosely, stir halfway and check several spots reach 165 F (74 C). Store any fresh crunchy garnishes separately and add them only after reheating.

Check broth and hominy labels for allergens or sulfites. Pepitas are pumpkin seeds. The blender and broth make this thicker than a clear chicken soup; actual finished volume depends on evaporation, so divide by six equal portions rather than an assumed cup yield.
Developed and reviewed in writing; not yet kitchen-tested. Numerical nutrition estimates are not published because final product labels and a complete calculation have not been verified.
